summary: Continue the beyond-AAA stewardship goal by addressing the measured client frame-time seam without reducing authored visual identity or changing the frozen gameplay contract.

A repeated active Null Foundry Redline workload measured 41.12 ms average / 62.5 ms p95 requestAnimationFrame cadence, but frame deltas alone could not identify Canvas work versus preview scheduling delay.

Bounded diagnostics were added for Canvas render duration, track/actor/effect/audio stages, HUD update duration, authority packet cadence, interpolation activity, pose snaps, and scheduling wait under named workloads.

Active race and battle render work remained under 3.3 ms p95 and HUD work under 1.2 ms p95 while preview frame p95 remained 34.9 to 55.6 ms. The local preview was classified scheduler-limited rather than Canvas-bound.

v0.11 adds presentation-only authority-packet pose interpolation: positions follow bounded linear paths, heading uses the shortest wrap-safe arc, and jumps over 180 world pixels snap immediately. No authoritative packet or gameplay state is mutated.
The presentation-pipeline soak passed 45,504 interpolated poses and 864 injected teleport snaps with a maximum 36-world-pixel ordinary step and zero prior/current packet mutation.

Fresh v0.11 Redline preserved the complete 1280x720 lobby and active Foundry pressure scene, accrued 74 interpolation frames with zero snaps, and measured 1.44 ms average / 3.3 ms p95 render work plus 0.55 / 0.8 ms HUD work at approximately 91.6 ms authority packets.

Isolated active Mirror Core preserved its complete arena and combat HUD, accrued 224 interpolation frames with zero snaps, and measured 1.41 ms average / 2.8 ms p95 render work at approximately 91.2 ms authority packets.

The browser exposed repeated still frames but no ephemeral rolling buffer. Preserved composition and active interpolation state pass; perceived high-cadence smoothness remains unknown pending target-display observation.
Package and health metadata advanced to PLAYABLE ALPHA V11 · PRESENTATION PIPELINE PASS / 0.11.0 while the whole-product release status remains alpha.

npm.cmd test passed 32 focused checks, the presentation-pipeline soak, 24 default races, 36 cross-track races, 72 track/variant races, 32 battles, 30 virtual reliability minutes, restart recovery, and HTTP contracts; final heap delta was 6.3 MB.

The regenerated comparator reports zero missing declared capabilities and overall UNKNOWN. Local render-work and interpolation capabilities are available; end-to-end frame budget, hardware soak, human presentation/audio judgment, physical LAN, and steward approval remain degraded or unknown.
MIRRORSHIFT package verification returned zero errors and one expected physical-phone warning; verifier selftest passed 15 assertions and all package JSON parsed.

The broad verifier could not complete because concurrently created foreign lane 018-last-stop-nebula had runtime files but no game.manifest.json. Snapshot evidence classified this as MOVING_WORKSPACE; no foreign files were edited.

The wider goal stays active. Next evidence priorities are target-hardware frame pacing and high-cadence observation, four physical-phone LAN, human listening/mix and character attachment, then additional animation, voice, and content breadth.
